newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- SING TAO -- China accused dissident Wang Xizhe of leaving the country for the U.S. illegally and said it would punish him and his collaborators.
-- Bejing-funded WEN WEI PO -- China's premier hosted the opening ceremony of the 80th Canton Trade Fair and said the Chinese economy would be stronger next year.
-- COMMERCIAL DAILY -- China is willing to provide credit to overseas buyers to support its exports of machines and equipment.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The People's Bank of China has decided to lift credit limits for circulating capital for banks early next year. It would be an important step towards commercialising Chinese banks.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Sun Hung Kei Co plans to raise $498 million by issuing more shares to present shareholders.
-- MING PAO -- A new product of a wine factory in Henan province, "Three Milk Wine", claimed to be made from the milk of cows, goats and humans, but turned out to be a hoax.
-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Former ICAC boss Jim Buckle got an apology and $500,000 from ATV after being libelled on a news show by a former friend and colleague.
-- The China World Trade Centre, a huge Beijing hotel and
commercial complex, was seeking to raise up to US$200 million through an initial public offering in Hong Kong late next year.

-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Special Administrative Region Land Fund had already surpassed the $100 billion that mainland officials had expected it to be worth at the time of the handover.
-- China plans to issue rules on build-operate-transfer projects to promote their use in the key power industry. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843-6441
GOLD - Yet another stolid performance in store for gold on Wednesday, though prices may drift towards support at $380.00 amid the lack of significant two-way business, traders and analysts said.
"There is little going on...any easing in the market will only reflect the general lack of interest," one trader commented.
Traders said volumes have remained thin and expect this condition to continue amid the lack of market-related news for the remainder of the week.
At 0730 spot gold was quoted at $380.70/381.20, against Tuesday's London close of $381.20/$381.70.
Analysts said a break below $380 could see prices ease to $378/$379, followed by the October 1 low of $376.90.
On the charts traders noted a minor downtrend line joining the highs of October 10, 14 and 15.
In early trading this line was offering light resistance around $381.20.
On the upside initial resistance was pegged at $382, then $383 and $385.
SILVER - Likely to test lower levels and could possibly test the October 10 low of $4.94 if initial support around $4.98 is breached.
On the charts the 10-day moving averge at $4.95 was about to make an upside cross on the downtrending 30-day indicator, currently around $4.98, analysts noted.
Resistance is expected to emerge from Tuesday's high of $5.06, followed by the recent peak at $5.09.
At 0752 GMT spot silver was quoted at $5.01/5.03, little changed.

PALLADIUM - Unmoved in early trading at $116.00/$117.00, though recent strong downside pressure likely to continue against the backdrop of sales from producer Russia and a lack of physical offtake from the Japanese electronics industry.
Several traders suggest prices have the potential to fall to $112 support and possibly below $100 an ounce.
PLATINUM - Range-bound between $380 and $385.
